question: Does the independently sampled 2017-2019 Azores native forest trail system show different native-vs-introduced plant composition at trail edges versus comparable interior samples, when the nested trail-area-plot-line sampling design and effort are respected?

physical_sample_fixed.units: 3 shared 50/100/150cm line Event observations per original 2x10m physical plot, aggregated before analysis
physical_sample_fixed.line_match_rule: Use only source-only v1.294 eligible matched trail×year×area groups; edge physical plot1 contrasted with interior physical plots2/3 if they each have full common 50/100/150 lines
physical_sample_fixed.line25: Never include, because no corresponding interior 25cm line
physical_sample_fixed.unknown_event_codes: Retain source-only v1.294 structural exclusions unchanged; NEVER change group after seeing plant outcomes
physical_sample_fixed.study_block: trail (4 published, three Terceira, one São Miguel); trail×area repeated sampling is not independent island replication
physical_sample_fixed.origin_status: Normalize exact DarwinCore establishmentMeans values native/indigenous/endemic/azorean endemic/native nonendemic as native; introduced/invasive/naturalized/naturalised as introduced. Other/uncertain/mixed -> unknown/exclude. No posthoc status reclassification
physical_sample_fixed.eligible_taxon: scientificName non-empty and exact taxonRank species; allow original species-level author name unchanged as identity; same physical plot×species counts once even if on multiple lines; count species across all three identical line positions, not 10 subpoint records as independent

primary.plot_log_native_intro_ratio: log((number native taxa + 0.5)/(number introduced taxa + 0.5)) using source's 3 shared line-position detections in physical plots
primary.within_group_effect: interior plot average log ratio minus edge plot log ratio for each matched trail×year×area group
primary.independent_trail_summary: Average group effects within each trail; report four or fewer trail results and per-island mean with original number of physically observed trails
primary.direction: positive interior-minus-edge indicates relative native-plant enrichment within native forest along trail edge compared with matched interior
primary.inference: Descriptive only; with one trail on São Miguel, a significance claim across islands is invalid; report how many independent trails show positive direction, no p-values, CI or pseudo-independent line-level testing
primary.secondary: Report separate per-trail native-richness and introduced-richness interior/edge differences plus original authors' source sampling coverage, status ambiguity rates; no historical-loss case selection after seeing response
primary.not_estimate: Recolonization, demographic rescue, invasive-plant causal suppression, vegetation recovery, disturbance intervention, randomization or independent archipelago replication

effect_emission_gate: Do not compute numeric primary contrast unless all v1.294 physical and v1.295 biological status/join/effort gates pass. On any STOP emit null score and preserve independent original source lineage.
prior_art: Trail authors explicitly designed this survey for tourism-associated vegetation disturbance, and general native-vs-invasive contrasts are not guaranteed novel. The new question is quantitative edge-versus-interior native/alien composition under matched original plot and line sampling, and comparison of potentially distinct island contexts.
